name: Stephen Hawking
kicker: British theoretical physicist · Black holes and A Brief History of Time
briefing: Stephen Hawking spent most of his career exploring black holes and the origin of the universe from a wheelchair, after a motor neuron disease gradually took away his ability to walk and, eventually, to speak without help. He proposed that black holes slowly leak radiation and could eventually evaporate entirely, and his 1988 book _A Brief History of Time_ turned complex cosmology into a surprise bestseller that sold millions of copies.

sample.note: 4 real QBReader tossups (2 Middle School/Easy High School + 2 Regular High School, power-marked)

tossups.p: This man lost a bet with physicist Kip Thorne over whether Cygnus X-1 [“SIG-nus”] contains a black hole, paying off with a subscription to a magazine. He later lost a separate bet with John Preskill about the black hole information paradox, settling that one with a baseball encyclopedia.
tossups.r: This physicist proposed that black holes slowly leak a namesake form of radiation and could eventually evaporate completely. For 10 points, name this British cosmologist who wrote _A Brief History of Time_.

tossups.p: This man’s 1966 doctoral thesis at Cambridge helped establish that the universe must have begun from a singularity, building on earlier work he later extended with Roger Penrose into a joint theorem. He also proposed a “no-boundary” model of the universe’s origin together with physicist Jim Hartle.
tossups.r: In 2009, he hosted a party for time travelers but mailed out the invitations only afterward, so that only a true time traveler could attend. For 10 points, name this physicist who used a wheelchair and a computer-generated voice.

tossups.p: This man earned a first-class degree in physics from Oxford before moving to Cambridge for graduate study, where he later held the Lucasian Professor of Mathematics chair starting in 1979, a position once held by Isaac Newton. His namesake radiation raises an “information paradox” about whether information swallowed by a black hole is truly lost forever.
tossups.r: Diagnosed with motor neuron disease at just 21 years old, this man was given only a couple of years to live but survived for over five more decades. For 10 points, name this physicist, the author of _A Brief History of Time_.

tossups.p: After a tracheotomy, this man selected words using small cheek muscle movements detected by a sensor on his glasses, composing sentences at a slow but steady rate. He received the Presidential Medal of Freedom from Barack Obama in 2009.
tossups.r: This physicist also wrote popular science books for young readers, including _George’s Secret Key to the Universe_. For 10 points, name this wheelchair-using cosmologist known for his work on black holes.

tossups.p: This man appeared as himself in episodes of _The Simpsons_ and _Star Trek: The Next Generation_. He proposed, with Jim Hartle, a “no-boundary” model suggesting the universe has no distinct starting edge in time.
tossups.r: This physicist died in March 2018 at age 76, decades after being diagnosed with a motor neuron disease often called Lou Gehrig’s disease. For 10 points, name this British scientist known for his work on black holes and _A Brief History of Time_.

trap.title: Hawking, Penrose, or black holes?
trap.body: Many clues about this physicist mention black holes, singularities, and Roger Penrose, because the two worked together and because his most famous theoretical work was about black holes — but “black holes” and “Roger Penrose” are each their own, separate answers. A tossup built entirely around the Penrose-Hawking singularity theorems could in theory be hunting for either collaborator’s name.
trap.fix: Listen for a biographical giveaway unique to one man: a wheelchair, ALS, a voice synthesizer, or _A Brief History of Time_ point to this physicist specifically, not to Penrose or to black holes in general.
